newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: AIOC Caspian oil group sticks to August start date.
newsitem.headline: AIOC Caspian oil group sticks to August start date.

text.p: A giant consortium of Western energy firms developing Azerbaijan's offshore Caspian Sea oilfields should be able to meet its initial production target, an official at Azeri state oil company SOCAR said on Tuesday.

Ilkham Aliyev, a SOCAR vice-president, told reporters he expected the Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) to begin producing oil from one of its three offshore platforms on August 28 as planned.
"(AIOC President) Terry Adams told me they would meet the appointed date," Aliyev said. "So we are hoping for that."

Some technical problems in laying a pipeline from the Azeri shore to the Chirag field, one of three sites involved, and poor weather have led to speculation in Baku that the production date could be moved back.
The $8 billion, 13-member AIOC consortium is led by British Petroleum and Statoil (Den norse stats oljeselskap) .
Other members are Amoco Corp, Unocal Corp, Russia's LUKoil, Pennzoil Co., Turkish Petroleum, Japan's Itochu, Ramco Energy Plc, Exxon Corp and Saudi Arabia's Delta Nimir.
SOCAR has a 10 percent stake. The Azeri goverment says it will receive more than 70 percent of the proceeds from the project over its 30-year life.
AIOC officials will make a recommendation to the Azeri government on June 12 on where to build a major new export pipeline to carry oil from output which is expected to peak in 2005.
AIOC's three offshore fields are estimated to hold over 500 million tonnes of oil and 55 billion cubic meters of natural gas.
So-called early oil will be exported via existing routes through Russia to its Black Sea port of Novorossiisk and via Georgia's Black Sea outlet at Supsa.
The AIOC project, considered the largest of its kind in the former Soviet Union, will see initial output of around 100,000 bpd, rising to 700,000-800,000 bpd by 2010.
